segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Aakashvani and I am Shagun Chopra with the Midday News.
The headlines
Seven people arrested in connection with stampede at a puja pandal in Kolkata, Prime Minister
Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Suvindwadhikari announced ex-Gresha.
In Gwalior, 14 people killed, 39 injured as truck plows into outer wall of Shethlamatha
Temple. Mass protests sweep Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal over rising cost of
living, stagnant wages and housing affordability, mounting pressure on EU governments.
The Indian Embassy in Riyadh urges Indian nationals to follow safety directives amid
continued conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthis.
IMD issues read alert for extremely heavy rainfall in coastal Andhra Pradesh for today, heavy
rain expected in Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu till tomorrow.
Asian Paragames 2026 to commence in Japan's IIT Nagoya in a short while from now with
Pramod Bhagat and Simran Sharma to carry India's flag at the opening ceremony.
And now the news in detail.
In West Bengal, 19 people lost their lives and 25 others were injured in a stampede at
the Turbhagan Durga Puja Pandal in North Kolkata last evening.
The incident occurred at around 8 p.m. during the Mahasaptami celebrations.
According to police and eyewitnesses, heavy rain and a sudden rush of visitors led
to chaos at the crowded pandal.
In the wake of the tragic incident at Chorbhagan, Kolkata police have imposed prohibitory orders
under Section 163 of the Bharti and Nagrik Suraksha Sahita in a large area surrounding
Chorbhagan, including Central Avenue, for the next three days.
Gatherings of five or more people, processions, public meetings and the carrying of dangerous
weapons are banned.
Police say the move follows intelligence inputs warning of a possible law and
order problem.
Meanwhile, Girish Park police have registered a case and launched an investigation to determine
the cause of the Turbhagan incident and fix responsibility.
In the meantime, Kolkata police today arrested seven people in connection with the stampede
at the Turbhagan Sarbha Jonyan Durgotsav, Samiti Durga Pooja Pandal.
West Bengal Chief Minister Subindu Adhikari has announced the formation of a high-level
Committee to review safety arrangements at Major Durga Puja Pandals across the state following
the deadly stampede. The Committee will review crowd management, emergency exit routes and
structural safety at prominent Puja venues and recommend measures to prevent similar
incidents in the future.
The Chief Minister has directed organisers to strictly follow the safety guidelines issued
by the authorities, emphasising that public safety must take precedence over elaborate
pandal designs and themes.
President Draupadi Murmur Vice President CP Radha Krishnan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi
and other senior leaders have expressed deep sorrow over the loss of lives in the stampede
in Kolkata.
Prime Minister Modi has announced an excretion of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister's
National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each person who lost their lives in the
stampede.
The injured will receive 50,000 rupees each.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Chief Minister Suvindwadikari and took stock of the
situation following the stampede.
In Madhya Pradesh, 12 people were killed and 39 others injured after an out-of-control
truck crashed into the outer wall of the Sheet-La-Mata Temple on Channur Road in Gwalior
last night.
The vehicle reported broke through police barricades, rolled down a steep slope and
plowed into devotees gathered on the road, crushing several pilgrims before coming
to a halt.
President Draupadi Murmu and Vice President CP Radha Krishnan have expressed condolences
on the loss of lives in a road accident in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
In a social media post, the President has prayed for the swift recovery of those injured.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi also expressed grief at the mishap.
Mr. Modi has announced an excretion of Rs. 2 lakh from the Prime Minister's National
Relief Fund for the next skin of each of those who lost their lives and Rs. 50,000
for those injured.
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority under the Department of Pharmaceuticals has
undertaken trade margin rationalization or TMR for 137 identified, non-scheduled anti-cancer
drugs in the public interest.
The initiative aims to curb excessive trade margins, make cancer treatment more affordable,
and improve access to anti-cancer medicines.
The move is expected to reduce the maximum retail prices, MRPs, of the identified
medicines by up to 70%, depending on their existing price structures. The Ministry of
Chemicals and Fertilizers has said that the revised prices will come into effect on 9th
of next month. Consumers can check the revised prices of medicines through the Pharma Saheedam
app at the MPPA website.
The newly appointed Governor of Odisha, Braj Mohan Ram, today took oath of office and
secrecy at a ceremony held at Lok Bhavan in Bhuvaneshwar. Chief Justice of the
Justice Harish Tandon administered the oath through the new governor in the presence of
Chief Minister Mohan Charanmajhi, Union Minister Duelo Ram, Speaker of the Odisha Legislative
Assembly Surama Padhi, Council of Ministers and Senior State Government Officials.
Bhraj Mohan Ram succeeds Dr. Hari Babu, Kam Bhapati, as the Governor of Odisha.
He was appointed to the constitutional post by President Draupadi Murmur on 12th of
this month.
Ram is a former three-time member of parliament from Palamu in Charkhand. His
wearing in marks the formal beginning of his tenure as the constitutional head of
Odisha. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe in Tajikistan to
represent India at the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government of the
Shanghai Cooperation Organization or SEO. The two-day meeting will start
tomorrow. The Defence Ministry said that the meeting will focus on
strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO member states, particularly in the areas
of trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural humanitarian exchanges.
It added that the meeting is expected to review the progress of ongoing cooperation initiatives
and consider decisions regarding the organization's financial and institutional functioning.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
For news at your fingertips follow us on X at AIR news alerts and join our WhatsApp channel
Aakashwani News.
Welcome back you are listening to midday news.
Durga puja celebrations have gripped Odisha with devotees thronging temples and beautifully
decorated puja pandals across the state, a report.
The festive spirit of Durga Puja has reached a crescendo across Odisha as thousands of
devotees gather at temples and elaborately decorated pendels to offer prayers to Ma Durga.
From the early morning hours, the air has resonated with devotional chants, the rhythmic
beats of traditional drums, and the sound of conch cells creating an atmosphere of
deep faith and spiritual fervour, while special Maha Astami rituals are being performed
At Sakthi Feet, across the state, Mahasattami Pooja is under way at Durga Pooja Pendals,
where priests are conducting traditional ceremonies and devotees are seeking the blessings of the
Divine Mother.
In Bhubaneswar and Katak, magnificent decorations, artistic installations and dazzling illuminations
have added grandeur to the celebrations.
Authorities have put special security and traffic arrangements in place at several
locations to regulate crowds and facilitate smooth darshan.
Prakash Das, Hakaaswani News, Bhuvaneswar.
Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across Belgium, France, Italy
and Portugal to protest against rising living costs, low wages and the growing difficulty
of accessing affordable housing.
The demonstrations have put governments across the European Union under pressure.
France witnessed widespread unrest with more than 5,50,000 people participating in
demonstrations according to the Interior Ministry.
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lycault-New said around 1,200 people had been arrested
and 150 police officers injured. Dozens of shops were looted in several cities including
Paris, Marseille, Nice, Bordeaux and Toulouse. In Limousies, a fire set by mass protesters
largely destroyed the historic town hall, French President Emmanuel Macron vowed that
those responsible would be prosecuted. In Belgium, police used tear gas and water
cannon to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liege, following reports of projectiles
being thrown at officers and fires being set.
Meanwhile, tens of thousands of people reportedly marched in Portugal's capital, Lisbon, protesting
against rising living costs, low wages and soaring housing prices.
Portuguese Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos Abreu Amorim said the government would
not yield to pressure from street demonstrations while protesters accused political leaders
of being out of touch with their concerns. In Italy, demonstrations in Milan against
wars and rising living costs turned violent, with protesters clashing with police, looting
shops and setting fire to barricades. Police used air gas and water cannon to disperse
the crowds. Italian Prime Minister, George Amaloni, condemned the violence, saying that
while demonstrating was a right, setting cities ablaze was unacceptable.
Saudi Arabia says it has intercepted and destroyed four drones over Riyadh, the
eastern province and southern regions as Houthi attacks continue.
In a separate incident, two crew members were killed when a reconnaissance helicopter
crashed in the kingdom's Najran region due to a technical malfunction, according to the
Saudi-elite coalition.
Meanwhile, Egypt is preparing to discuss potential support for Saudi Arabia's defenses
with parliaments set to hold an emergency session on Sunday, after President Abdel Fateh
LCC sought authorization to provide assistance if requested by Riyadh.
Separately, a tugboat travelling south near the UAE's Khorkhan reported being struck by
two unidentified projectiles, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations Agency.
In Yemen, Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for a missile attack on Aden International
Airport on Friday.
The vessel sustained damage and one person suffered minor injuries, but the tug continued
on its route. An LNG tanker of Yemen's Mukalla also reported coming down under fire, gunfire
from people aboard a small skiff.
The conflict in Yemen involving Saudi Arabia and Houthis continues to threaten civilian infrastructure
including airports. Major Indian airlines have suspended operations to various Saudi
airports until October 24. Meanwhile, maritime traffic around both Strait of Hormuz and
Red Sea route remains under pressure. Security reports recorded a spike in incidents
events during the first half of October, with six vessels targeted on Oct. 11 alone.
And with the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports continuing, mid-time traffic, particularly
energy shipments through the region, remain significantly disrupted.
Manish Shiva, Akashwani News, Dubai.
The Indian Embassy in Riyadh today urged Indian nationals to follow Saudi safety directives
amid security concerns following Houthi drone and missile attacks.
The advisory asks people to shelter indoors, stay away from windows and open areas, avoid
filming incidents and follow official alerts. Motorists have been advised to stop away from
bridges and high-rise buildings. For emergencies, people can call 9-1-1 in Makkah, Medina, Riyadh
and the eastern province and 9-9-8 in other parts of Saudi Arabia. The advisory follows
a drone and missile attack on Riyadh's King Khaled international airport on October 10th
that killed an Indian national and injured several others.
U.S. President Donald Trump has suspended several sanctions targeting Russia just two
days before they were due to take effect amid growing tensions with Ukrainian President
Volodymyr Zelensky.
Mr Trump issued an executive order on Friday stating that suspending certain sanctions
was in the national interest of the United States.
U.S. Secretary of State Mark Rubio yesterday said that the suspension will consist
of a 60-day pause intended to analyze the impact on the global economy.
The move has drawn criticism from U.S. lawmakers as the sanctions has been approved by Congress
and signed into law in September.
The India Meteorological Department, IMD, has issued a red-colour warning for very heavy
rainfall to extremely heavy rainfall over coastal Andhra Pradesh for the day.
Heavy rainfall is also expected over Kerala, Mahi, South Indira, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu,
Puducherry and Karayakul till tomorrow.
The med department said that thunderstorms and lightning conditions will continue over
Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada and Lakshadweep till tomorrow.
The Asian Paragames 2026 will officially open at Aichi Nagoya in Japan today, with India
aiming to build on its record medal hall at the previous edition.
The opening ceremony today will be held at the Paloma Mizohu Stadium in Nagoya under
the theme Vabi.
We are beautiful individuals.
The ceremony will begin at 2.30 PM Indian Standard Time, several competitions including
During blind football, Parabatminton, Paratable tennis are scheduled to begin before the opening
ceremony.
Parabatminton player Pramod Bhagat and sprinter Simran Sharma will lead the Indian contingent
as flag bearers during the ceremony.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again, 7 people arrested in connection
with stampede at a puja pandal in Kolkata, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Ministers
Vindu Adhikari announced ex-Gracia. In Gwalior, 14 people killed, 39 other injured as truck
plows into outer wall of Sheetla Mata Temple.
Mass protests, we Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal over rising cost of living, stagnant
wages and housing affordability, mounting pressure on EU governments. The Indian MSC
in Riyadh urges Indian nationals to follow safety directors amid continued conflict
between Saudi Arabia and Houthis. Asian Paragames 2026 to commence in Japan's
to Nagoya in a short while from now, with Pramod Bhagatan's Simran Sharma to carry
India's flag at opening ceremony.
And with that, we end the mid-day news.
